authors_of_unit.name: Stephanie D. Preston
authors_of_unit.key_prior_work: The Altruistic Brain (Oxford 2014); Preston & de Waal 'Altruism' (Handbook of Social Neuroscience, 2011); Preston & Hofelich 'The Many Faces of Empathy' (Emotion Review 4.1, 2012)
authors_of_unit.met_gross_at: University of Iowa, 2003 (preparing 'The Promise of Empathy' conference)

first_publication: Earlier version in Frank Biess + Daniel M. Gross (eds.), Science and Emotion after 1945: A Transatlantic Perspective (Chicago 2014)
special_features: Continuous prose with THREE internal subheadings: 'Limits of Laboratory Science of Emotion' (PDF 141 / book 131), 'Fear Situated' (PDF 147 / book 137), 'Empathy Situated' (PDF 152 / book 142), 'Summary and Conclusion' (PDF 154 / book 144)
Co-authored — every edge must carry contributor field (Gross / Preston / Gross & Preston)
Frames volume around C. P. Snow 'The Two Cultures' (1959)
Centers on Elizabeth A. Phelps lab fMRI/race study (J. Cognitive Neuroscience 12.5, 2000) as test object
Closes the volume with a methodological reflection rather than a fifth literary reading
42 endnotes — heaviest note apparatus in the volume; bibliography spans neuroscience methodology critique, critical neuroscience, and history of emotions

outline.heading: [Headnote: title + 'With Stephanie Preston' byline]
outline.function: Establishes co-authorship structure (Gross primary; Preston joint)

outline.heading: [Unheaded opening — Snow framing + two-cultures responses]
tags: C. P. Snow 'The Two Cultures' Rede Lecture (1959)
controlled-laboratory vs. natural-complexity opposition
emotion as a fundamental human phenomenon that crosses the divide
'emotional turn' since 1980s rise of neuroimaging
Response 1: incommensurability (Scarantino + Griffiths' Folk vs. Scientific Emotion Project distinction; Carolyn J. Dean on Einfühlung 1873 and post-Holocaust empathy exhaustion)
Response 2: consilience (E. O. Wilson; Steven Pinker reading Austen's Sense and Sensibility via evolutionary psychology + Robert Trivers' 'moral emotions')
Gross & Preston's third move: dissolution of the two-culture problem, not a third response
Reverse inference problem as historical-methodological marker

outline.heading: Limits of Laboratory Science of Emotion
tags: Eight-point critique of fMRI/PET/TMS/EEG/ERP/MEG laboratory neuroscience
1) Technological limitations (machine noise + immobility; few-second visual/audio stimuli; money as crude dependent measure)
2) Money and the limitation of a utilitarian assumption (linear-valuation problem; money mindset suppresses prosociality)
3) Professional journal impact factor (oversimplification incentive; 'Brain region found for the unique human ability to read minds')
4) Mass media attention (data-fabrication scandals; oversimplified claims travel fastest)
5) Localization ('social brain,' 'empathy circuit,' 'self-related regions' as misleading shorthand)
6) Limits of professional expertise (single-discipline reading blocks cross-disciplinary inference — angular gyrus example: arithmetic / metaphor / out-of-body / cross-modal / self-relevant)
7) Reverse inference limitations (Russell Poldrack critique; DLPFC + working-memory inference; functional localizer + Theory-of-Mind 'Sally' task; insula + Preston-lab acquisitiveness study)
8) Technocratic hierarchy (~$600/subject, $12,000+/experiment, $100,000+ infrastructure)
Broadmann (1909) cytoarchitectural numbering
Equiano 'happy' situation (Ch. 2 callback) as durable social affordance the scanner cannot register
Korbinian Broadmann, Russell Poldrack, John M. Wang et al. (Preston lab), Antonio Damasio, Hannah Faye Chua

outline.heading: Fear Situated
tags: Central historical claim: emotional topics of laboratory work coincide with socio-historical concerns at margins of experiment design and interpretation
Wittgenstein + Vygotsky + Heideggerian phenomenological lineage; J. J. Gibson ecological perception
Case 1: 'fear' in Phelps + Barsalou laboratories — post-war concern with racism
Case 2: 'empathy' in Preston laboratory + colleagues — post-war concern with humanitarianism
Phelps et al. 2000 (J. Cog. Neuroscience 12.5, 729–738): fMRI study of White American responses to Black/White faces
Experiment 1: unfamiliar Black/White faces — amygdala activity correlated with Modern Racism Scale + startle-response measures of unconscious bias (p. 729, 730, 736)

Experiment 2: famous + positively regarded faces (Arsenio Hall, Bill Cosby, Magic Johnson, MLK Jr., Colin Powell vs. Conan O'Brien, Tom Cruise, Larry Bird, JFK, Norman Schwarzkopf) — pattern not reproduced (p. 730, 734, 736)
Phelps's qualification: 'these data cannot speak to the issues of causality' (734); 'history of relations between social groups' is the operative context
Gross's rhetorical-historical reframing: racism is located primarily in institutions (US race-based slavery; Jim Crow) not in brain physiology
Critique of 'familiarity' construct in Experiment 2 — Arsenio Hall recognized via televisual mediation, NOT face-to-face acquaintance; familiarity vs. celebrity-as-mediation
MLK Jr. vs. JFK as 'roughly equivalent' images conceals uneven distribution of fame and markedness across Black and White populations
Barsalou + Wilson-Mendenhall 'Grounding Emotion in Situated Conceptualization' (2011) critiques Ekman basic-emotion approach (snake/fear circuit at 1105)
Runner-on-trail-at-dusk fear vs. presentation-fear: dorsolateral prefrontal + inferior frontal gyrus (1124)
Limits of Barsalou's modular-functionalist framing — falls back on elliptical 'and so forth' for non-conceptual social affordances
Griffiths + Scarantino 'emotions in the wild' (438, 441) — Vygotskian synchronic scaffolding + diachronic scaffolding (confessional / Catholic culture, 443); emotional capital (444)
Critical race theory + rhetorical studies as the missing 'mediating field of socio-historical phenomena'
Preview of Preston Ecological Neuroscience Lab as exemplary integrative model

outline.heading: Empathy Situated
tags: Critique of mirror-neuron account of empathy as circular (non-cognitive trans-primate; empathy = mirror-neuron activity = empathy)
Preston + Hofelich case studies of videoed hospital patients with serious/terminal illness
Empathy / apathy / RETICENCE triad (Preston's signal contribution)
Variance pattern: observers experiencing depression-driven negative affect report LESS sympathy for distraught patients
Observers who 'take another's perspective' regularly report MORE sympathy for the reticent patient
Carolyn J. Dean: post-WWII Holocaust-victim testimony genre — reticence as marker of 'authentic' suffering, false-victim discourse
Dean: 'The preference for minimalist style in victim testimonies… is but one component of a much broader discourse about the exemplary victim' (396)
Disanalogy between Preston-lab patients (reticent receive LEAST sympathy) and Dean's survivors (reticent are most credible)
Both cases reveal the same methodological injunction: empathy research must be located in particular historical/cultural situations
Gender expectations in the Preston hospital study — differential help for distraught vs. resilient patients
'Anxiety of transmission' in the historian-audience reception of survivor tales
Humanities construction of dignity: how victims of systematic oppression OR 'natural' circumstances are constituted, alongside agencies expected to respond

outline.heading: Summary and Conclusion
tags: Two responses to two-cultures impasse: explained-by-incommensurability vs. addressed-by-consilience (E. O. Wilson reductive tradition)
Gross & Preston's wager: experiments can proceed more ecologically and yield brain-body-world insights

Mutual obligations: scientists must build ecological + situated + statistically powerful protocols; humanists must refuse the all-or-none proposition (racial hatred / empathy / self either fully experimentally available OR fully unavailable)
Two-cultures collaboration as 'early stages' — situated cognition as the invitational framework
Cognition without neuroscience is misleading; science without humanities-situational concerns lacks its environmental dimension
'Situations' are environmental — including social environments quite specific like empathy exhaustion (Dean) and historical (Reddy adjacency)
Qualified-NO answer to Snow: the dichotomy DISSOLVES when human emotions are treated with methodological diversity

concepts.label: two cultures (Snow)
concepts.gloss: C. P. Snow's 1959 Rede Lecture diagnosis of the chasm between scientific and humanistic intellectual cultures; the operative frame for the entire Epilogue

concepts.label: irreconcilable difference
concepts.gloss: Titular question; the chapter answers with a qualified 'No' — the dichotomy is reconcilable only via rhetorical-situational reframing

concepts.label: the 'emotional turn'
concepts.gloss: Post-1980s reorientation of humanities and social sciences toward affect/emotion, intensified by the rise of neuroimaging

concepts.label: incommensurability response (to two-cultures)
concepts.gloss: First major response to Snow's divide: the fields are too field-specifically differentiated to be meaningfully compared; Scarantino & Griffiths' Folk-vs.-Scientific Emotion Project distinction is a semantic-theoretical corollary

concepts.label: consilience response (E. O. Wilson; Pinker)
concepts.gloss: Second major response: reductive integration under natural-scientific terms; Pinker reads Austen's Sense and Sensibility through evolutionary psychology + Trivers' 'moral emotions'

concepts.label: dissolution (not a third response) of the two-cultures problem
concepts.gloss: Gross & Preston's signature move: not a third response between incommensurability and consilience but a critique that DISSOLVES the problem when emotion is studied as a rhetorical-situational phenomenon

concepts.label: reverse inference (Poldrack 2006)
concepts.gloss: Methodological problem in neuroimaging: inferring that activation of a brain region in a new study implies the same cognitive process as a prior study; renders causal arguments in neuroscience suspect

concepts.label: situated cognition
concepts.gloss: Recent psychology / neuroscience approach (Barsalou, Barrett) compatible with humanities + interpretive social science; the volume's invitational meta-frame

concepts.label: fMRI methodology (and its laboratory limits)
concepts.gloss: Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging — primary methodological object of critique; loud + immobilizing scanner forces few-second visual/audio stimuli, money as crude dependent measure

concepts.label: monetary-incentivization critique
concepts.gloss: Money as universal dependent measure problematic: non-linear value across persons and across individuals; specifically suppresses prosocial motives (altruism, empathy)

concepts.label: localization illusion ('social brain,' 'empathy circuit')
concepts.gloss: Misleading shorthand mapping specific tasks/functions to particular brain regions; the angular gyrus is variously construed as arithmetic / metaphor / out-of-body / cross-modal-integration / self-relevant area depending on the researcher's discipline

concepts.label: limits of professional expertise (cross-discipline inferential blockage)
concepts.gloss: Single-discipline reading habits prevent researchers from knowing that their 'pet' brain region is implicated in unrelated tasks studied in other fields, foreclosing accurate inferences

concepts.label: technocratic hierarchy of neuroscience funding
concepts.gloss: ~$600/subject, $12,000+/experiment, $100,000+ infrastructure with full-time staff — divides the field between heavily-funded labs and others who must use simpler techniques

concepts.label: central historical claim (laboratory topics coincide with socio-historical concerns)
concepts.gloss: 'The topics of laboratory work on the emotional brain coincide meaningfully with particular socio-historical concerns that show up at the margins of experiment design and interpretation' — fear→racism; empathy→humanitarianism

concepts.label: Phelps et al. 2000 fMRI race-amygdala study
concepts.gloss: Phelps et al., 'Performance on Indirect Measures of Race Evaluation Predicts Amygdala Activation,' Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience 12.5 (2000): 729–738. THE chief test object of the chapter

concepts.label: Modern Racism Scale (MRS)
concepts.gloss: Self-report questionnaire used by Phelps et al. to measure conscious racial attitudes; Phelps's amygdala correlation in Experiment 1 obtained against UNCONSCIOUS measures (startle, bias), NOT against the MRS

concepts.label: Phelps Experiment 1 (unfamiliar Black/White faces)
concepts.gloss: fMRI viewing of unfamiliar Black/White male faces with 'neutral' expressions; differential amygdala activity in White subjects correlated with UNCONSCIOUS (not conscious) race-evaluation measures

concepts.label: Phelps Experiment 2 (famous positively-regarded faces)
concepts.gloss: fMRI viewing of 'famous and positively regarded' faces — Arsenio Hall, Bill Cosby, Magic Johnson, MLK Jr., Colin Powell vs. Conan O'Brien, Tom Cruise, Larry Bird, JFK, Norman Schwarzkopf; the differential-amygdala pattern from Exp. 1 was NOT reproduced

concepts.label: rhetorical-situational reframing of neuroscience objects
concepts.gloss: Gross's signal contribution: even the most apparently biological fMRI findings only make sense when reframed as rhetorical-situational phenomena — Phelps's amygdala-correlate must be referred to 'racist institutions' (slavery, Jim Crow) that exceed any particular brain state

concepts.label: racism located primarily in institutions, not brains
concepts.gloss: 'Racism is not located primarily in the brain. It is located primarily in the racist institutions — like US race-based slavery and subsequent Jim Crow laws — that exceed any particular subject and can persist without any particular kind of incorporation or brain state'

concepts.label: 'familiarity' as televisual / capital mediation
concepts.gloss: Critique of Phelps's Exp. 2: 'familiarity' of Arsenio Hall's face for a White subject has nothing to do with face-to-face encounter, everything to do with regimes of publicity + capital; recall Equiano's 'familiarity' with slavemaster Henry Pascal (Ch. 2 callback)

concepts.label: markedness of Black vs. White celebrity
concepts.gloss: Fame and achievement are unevenly distributed across Black and White populations, so a famous Black face carries markedness into the lab that a 'roughly equivalent' famous White face does not — Phelps may be correlating CELEBRITY with unconscious racial attitudes

concepts.label: MLK Jr. / JFK as 'roughly equivalent' images
concepts.gloss: Phelps Exp. 2's stimulus pairing of MLK Jr. with JFK as 'roughly equivalent' in fame/age/achievement is itself a rhetorical-political claim about US public memory that the experimental design treats as given

concepts.label: basic-emotion approach critique (Ekman)
concepts.gloss: Wilson-Mendenhall, Barsalou et al. (2011) 'Grounding Emotion in Situated Conceptualization' critique Ekman's inborn-instinct + stereotyped-trigger model (e.g. snake → fear circuit at 1105)

concepts.label: situated conceptualization (Barsalou)
concepts.gloss: Emotions as concepts referring to entire situations representing settings, agents, objects, actions, events, interoceptions, mentalizings — fear-of-runner-lost-on-trail differs in instantiation from fear-of-presentation-at-work (DLPFC + inferior frontal gyrus, 1124)

concepts.label: Barsalou's elliptical-figures limit
concepts.gloss: Barsalou's modular-functionalist focus must rely on elliptical figures ('and so forth,' 'and many others') to articulate a background that recedes indefinitely into non-conceptual affordances of the social environment (Phelps's 'history of race relations')

concepts.label: 'emotions in the wild' (Griffiths + Scarantino)
concepts.gloss: Theoretical pivot from lab-restricted study to neglected phenomena: anger in marital quarrel, embarrassment in performance; environment represented in terms of what it AFFORDS the emoter (441)

concepts.label: synchronic + diachronic scaffolding (Griffiths + Scarantino)
concepts.gloss: Synchronic scaffolding after Vygotsky (e.g. confessional in church enables emotional performance); diachronic scaffolding (broader Catholic culture supporting development of confessional capacity); plus 'emotional capital' (444)

concepts.label: empathy / apathy / reticence triad
concepts.gloss: Preston's signal contribution: empathy is non-circularly definable only by including its negation (apathy) and the distinct third term reticence — quiet patients exhibiting minimal demonstrative emotion who nonetheless appear to have deep emotions and need

concepts.label: mirror-neuron account of empathy as circular
concepts.gloss: Mirror-neuron research casts empathy as non-cognitive trans-primate phenomenon (Iacoboni 2008); risks circularity in which empathy = mirror-neuron activity = empathy without explaining WHY certain actions elicit empathic responses and others do not

concepts.label: Preston + Hofelich hospital-patient video study
concepts.gloss: Hofelich PhD dissertation (Michigan 2012) + Preston: videos of real seriously/terminally ill patients discussing illness; observer reactions vary by observer's own depressive state and habitual perspective-taking

concepts.label: depression reduces sympathy for distraught patients
concepts.gloss: Preston-lab finding: observers experiencing their own intense negative affect due to depression report LESS sympathy for distraught patients — a context-sensitive structure that a mirror-neuron account cannot explain

concepts.label: perspective-takers prefer reticent patients
concepts.gloss: Preston-lab finding: observers who regularly 'take another's perspective' in daily life report GREATER sympathy for the reticent patient with deep underlying emotions/needs

concepts.label: Dean's post-WWII reticence-as-authenticity thesis
concepts.gloss: Carolyn J. Dean: in Holocaust survivor-testimony genre, reticence has become the marker of authentic suffering; false-victim discourse trumps inquiry into HOW victims are deemed credible; 'real' survivors are presumed reluctant to seek attention

concepts.label: Dean / Preston disanalogy on reticence
concepts.gloss: In Preston-lab hospital study, reticent patients receive the LEAST sympathy; in Dean's survivor archive, reticence is the marker of MAXIMAL credibility. The contrast itself shows that 'reticence' is not transparent across cultural/historical situations

concepts.label: gender expectations in empathy research
concepts.gloss: In Preston-Hofelich study, gender expectations play a key role in differential willingness to help distraught vs. resilient patients — empathy research cannot be gender-neutral without distorting its object

concepts.label: anxiety of transmission (survivor-tale reception)
concepts.gloss: In the reception of survivor's tale, anxiety about losing the subjects of study becomes prominent for historians and audiences — a humanities-side counterpart to the design-margin concerns at issue in lab studies

concepts.label: humanities construction of dignity
concepts.gloss: With Dean: a humanities account of how victims of systematic oppression or 'natural' circumstances are constituted along with the agencies supposed to respond — the construct that empathy-neuroscience cannot generate but cannot do without

concepts.label: methodological wager: two-cultures collaboration at early stages
concepts.gloss: Closing claim: 'we hope that this essay, written by a rhetorician and a neuroscientist, can serve as an example of two-cultures collaboration at its early stages. In situated cognition we identify an approach that invites such collaboration.' The volume's methodological self-justification

concepts.label: qualified 'No' answer to Snow
concepts.gloss: The volume's titular question 'Irreconcilable Differences?' is answered with a qualified No: the divide DISSOLVES when shared phenomena like human emotions are treated with methodological diversity and cross-disciplinary conversation

concepts.label: critical race theory + rhetorical studies as mediating field
concepts.gloss: Gross's proposed mediating field of socio-historical phenomena, drawing on critical race theory + rhetorical studies, that Phelps's protocol does not articulate sufficiently to shape laboratory work and its interpretation

concepts.label: ecological + situated + statistically powerful experimental protocols
concepts.gloss: Scientist-side obligation in the methodological treaty: design protocols within existing technological constraints that nonetheless register ecological and situational factors

concepts.label: refusal of the all-or-none proposition
concepts.gloss: Humanist-side obligation: refuse the demand that humanities topics (racial hatred, empathy, self) must be EITHER completely experimentally available OR completely unavailable; some experimental traction is possible without reductive capture

positions.claim: Snow's two-cultures dichotomy is the operative but contested frame for the volume; the Epilogue ultimately answers Snow's question with a qualified 'No' — the divide dissolves when emotion is studied with methodological diversity

The Phelps amygdala-race finding makes sense only when reframed as a rhetorical-situational object: racism is located in INSTITUTIONS (US race-based slavery, Jim Crow) that exceed any particular brain state, not primarily in brain physiology

The 'familiarity' variable in Phelps Experiment 2 has nothing to do with face-to-face acquaintance and everything to do with regimes of televisual publicity and capital — Phelps may be correlating CELEBRITY with unconscious racial attitudes, not familiarity per se

Empathy is properly understood only as one term in an empathy / apathy / reticence triad; the Preston-Hofelich hospital study and Dean's Holocaust-testimony archive together show that reticence functions differently in different cultural-historical situations

The mirror-neuron account of empathy is circular — empathy = mirror-neuron activity = empathy — and cannot explain why certain actions elicit empathic responses and others do not; case studies showing depression-driven reductions in sympathy and perspective-taking preferences for reticent patients break the circle

The brain-abstraction problem in contemporary fMRI/PET/TMS neuroscience is generated by eight interlocking limits: technological, monetary, journal-impact, mass-media, localization-illusion, professional-expertise, reverse-inference, and technocratic-hierarchy

Central historical thesis: the EMOTIONAL TOPICS of laboratory work coincide meaningfully with the socio-historical concerns that show up at the margins of experiment design and interpretation — fear-research in the Phelps/Barsalou labs aligns with post-war anti-racism; empathy-research in the Preston lab aligns with post-war humanitarianism

Methodological wager (volume self-justification): situated cognition is the framework that invites two-cultures collaboration at its early stages; cognition without neuroscience is misleading, science without humanities-situational concerns lacks its environmental dimension

E. O. Wilson / Pinker consilience is the wrong response to the two-cultures divide because it reads novelistic emotion (e.g. Austen's Sense and Sensibility) as evolutionary-psychological mating + Trivers's 'moral emotions' — sacrificing the local cultural texture that makes the object what it is

Barsalou's modular-functionalist situated-conceptualization is a necessary advance but is forced to rely on elliptical figures ('and so forth,' 'and many others') for the non-conceptual affordances that critical-race-theoretical and rhetorical analysis can specify

tensions.description: Incommensurability (Scarantino-Griffiths Folk vs. Scientific Emotion Project) vs. consilience (E. O. Wilson, Pinker) — the two dominant responses to Snow's divide, both of which Gross & Preston refuse
tensions.resolved: Dissolved via rhetorical-situational reframing — neither pure incommensurability nor reductive consilience

tensions.description: Titular sciences-vs-humanities tension — laboratory clean-controlled-results paradigm vs. humanities natural-complexity-with-cultural-frames paradigm — and whether emotion as a shared object can be jointly studied
tensions.resolved: Qualified-No answer to Snow: the divide dissolves under methodological diversity, but only if both sides accept their respective discipline-side obligations

tensions.description: Phelps et al. say 'these data cannot speak to the issues of causality' (734) but simultaneously place the data in 'the history of relations between social groups' — the protocol for connecting vague-history to concrete-neuroscientific-data is not articulated
tensions.resolved: Gross supplies the missing mediating field: critical race theory + rhetorical studies of socio-historical phenomena

tensions.description: Reticence functions OPPOSITELY in the Preston-lab hospital study (reticent patients receive LEAST sympathy) and Dean's Holocaust survivor archive (reticence is the marker of MAXIMAL authenticity/credibility)
tensions.resolved: The disanalogy itself proves the methodological point: 'reticence' is not transparent across cultural-historical situations and must be specified each time

tensions.description: Phelps Experiment 2's 'familiarity' construct equivocates between face-to-face acquaintance and televisual celebrity — the same surface variable conceals utterly different rhetorical-mediational structures (Arsenio Hall via TV vs. Equiano's familiarity with slavemaster Pascal)
tensions.resolved: Familiarity must be deployed with historical rigor — capital + publicity vs. interpersonal vs. forced-proximity slavery

tensions.description: Mirror-neuron / non-cognitive account of empathy vs. the demonstrable context-sensitivity of empathy (depressed observers report less sympathy; perspective-takers prefer reticent patients)
tensions.resolved: Case studies break the circular mirror-neuron account; empathy must be theorized as context-sensitive and situational

tensions.description: Tension between practical/political appeal of brain-localization claims ('the empathy circuit,' 'the social brain') and the empirical fact that any one region (e.g. angular gyrus) is implicated across many disciplinary task families
tensions.resolved: Cross-disciplinary inference + functional localizers; but rare in practice owing to technocratic and disciplinary hierarchies
